page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the running head above it. No marginal notes. A small asterisk stands in the left margin beside "ab origine". Below the last line, at the right, is the catchword "ei,".

main_text.p: quæ Cogitationibus nostris allubescunt. Eph. 2. 3. veterem Hominem. Rom. 6. 6. Concupiscentiam innatam. Jac. 1. 14, 15. Figmentum humani Cordis, malum ab ipla Juventute. Gen. 8. 21. & Carnem Spiritui obluctantem. Gal: 5. 17. Ipsam Conceptionem nostram Iniquitatis labe aspergit. Psal: 51. 5. Onagri pullo Hominem assimilat, cum primum generatur. Job: 11. 12. & Stultitiam in Corde Pueri colligatam esse affirmat, quam virga Correctionis expelli necesse est. Prov: 22. 15. Denique asserit Hominem animalem, (hoc est, Spiritu Dei destitutum) ii.orum omnino incapacem esse, quæ sunt Spiritus Dei, quia Stultitia ipsi videntur. 1, Cor: 2. 14. Eadem quoque Scriptura, Illuminationis gratiam, mentisque per Spiritum Dei renovatæ necessitatem passim inculcat, quibus hæc Dei Imago ab origine impressa, & posthac multum deturpata, denuo paulatim instauratur. Tertio; Adamum, per primum illud peccatum, se ipsamque naturam non corrupisse. Ita Socinus, in Prælect: cap: 4. Unum illud Peccatum per se, non modo miversos Posteros, sed ne ipsum quidem Adamum, corrumpendi vim habuit. & Catech. Rac. cap. 10 pag. 195. lapsu Adæ, cum unus Actus fuerit, vim eam, qua depravare ipsam naturam Adami, multo minus vero Posterorum ipsius posset, habere non potuit. At plane contrarium ex Antecedentibus liquet, quæ malignos istius peccati effectus plus satis manifestant, tum in Adami Persona spectandos, tum in ipsius posteris, qui ex illius natura post lapsum participarunt, præcipue vero, in persona ipsius Adami. Per istud enim factus est, ex Recto pravus, e Justo Injustus, e Puro & Sancto Pollutus, e libero Servus peccati, e Dei Filio Satanæ mancipium. Pudor item ex eo facto incuss

page.notes: The asterisk in the left margin beside "ab origine" is a printed reference mark with no text. The catchword "ei," at the foot may belong to a word broken as "incuss[i]ei"; the last line is partly covered, so the final letter of "incuss" is uncertain. The word "Peccatum" in the italic passage is printed with a letter that looks like V, and I read it as P. "Satanæ" is read with some doubt. "se ipsamque" in the line "se snamque" is uncertain. "ii.orum" and "ipla" are printed as shown. "1," after "videntur." is possibly a printed mark rather than a numeral. The phrase "Eph. 2. 3." has a 3 that may be a printed ȝ.
